complexity-reviewer.reason: complexity-reviewer measures firmware function size, responsibilities and nesting against the pipeline-stage idiom; code-simplifier looks for redundant abstractions and simpler equivalent code across firmware and Python tools. Different lenses on overlapping code.

clarity-reviewer.reason: Split by artifact: clarity-reviewer owns Markdown docs (staleness, duplication, wordiness); comment-analyzer owns code comments and docstrings. comment-analyzer's do-not-flag list excludes Markdown, and clarity-reviewer's excludes code comments.

tuning-layout-reviewer.reason: Split by layer: tuning-layout-reviewer owns the flash block contract (struct, version, CRC, UF2, packer/firmware parity); calibration-config-reviewer owns the per-unit values, their provenance and the capture/fit tooling.

hid-protocol-reviewer.reason: Both look at the main loop: hid-protocol-reviewer checks the TinyUSB contract (task() every iteration, one report per poll, pure-HID Serial fencing); realtime-loop-reviewer checks blocking and per-iteration cost. A stalled loop can be a finding for each, from a different cause.

sensor-i2c-reviewer.reason: sensor-i2c-reviewer counts I2C transactions and vendor retries; realtime-loop-reviewer judges their effect on loop latency. Each charter names the hand-off.

calibration-config-reviewer.reason: Both read tools/calibration/README.md and tools/config/README.md: calibration-config-reviewer checks the workflow still works end to end with the tools; clarity-reviewer checks staleness and wording.

memory-and-types-reviewer.reason: memory-and-types-reviewer covers alignment and size for all firmware; TuningConfig's own alignment and the image-below-0x101FE000 constraint belong to tuning-layout-reviewer, as memory-and-types-reviewer's charter says.
